prompt.text: New sign-in to your {{COMPANY}} account from {{CITY}}. Unknown browser. Was this you?

setup.speaker: Narrator
setup.text: Your phone buzzes on the desk. A sign-in alert for your Harbor account.

choices.label: Tap “Yes, it was me”
choices.bark: You approved it. Someone else is signed in as you.
choices.report: You approved a sign-in you didn't make.
choices.consequence_text: You tapped yes. Whoever that was is now signed in as you.
choices.debrief_text: You were right here, on fourteen. That sign-in came from somewhere else. Never approve one you didn't start. Tap no, then call security at extension 4400.

choices.label: Swipe it away
choices.bark: Dismissed. The session is still open.
choices.report: You swiped away a sign-in alert you didn't trigger and didn't report it.
choices.consequence_text: You swiped it away. The session stays open, and nobody is watching it.
choices.debrief_text: Not approving it helps. But a sign-in you didn't make means someone may have your password. Tap no, and report it, so security can shut it down.

choices.label: Tap “No, it wasn't me” and report it
choices.bark: Session killed. Security is resetting your password.
choices.report: You denied an unknown sign-in and reported it to security ({{SECURITY_PHONE}}).
choices.consequence_text: You tapped no and called it in. Security ended the session and reset your password.
choices.debrief_text: Exactly. A sign-in you didn't make is an incident, even at midnight. Tap no, then call security at extension 4400, or email security@harborandco.com.
